stories.US-B64-1: As an operator generating a project report over a manifest with declared regions, I get the report without the tool consuming memory proportional to (regions x variants x entries), so a large or hostile change document cannot exhaust my machine. READY.

design_decision: Option 2 — single-pass, region-indexed. Walk result->summary->entry/issue ONCE, decide region membership via range_index.py binary-search primitives, append into per-(region,class) BOUNDED buckets. O(VxE.logR + Rx3K) instead of O(RxVxE). Chosen over batch-63 per-hit-class cap because it also closes residual B-3(b) (a region matching fewer than the cap still traverses the full VxE, so an attacker declares R narrow zero-match regions and pays the full product for zero output). range_index.py is ENGINE-FROZEN but consuming it needs no unfreeze — verified, report_service.py imports it 0 times. HIGHEST-RISK UNKNOWN sent to Phase 1 as mandatory probe P-1: whether the range_index API allows recovering WHICH region an address fell into or only WHETHER it fell into any; if boolean-only, the frozen-safe fallback is a fast reject pre-filter plus a local bisect inside report_service.py.

phase1_result.design_correction_1: Per-class BUCKETS break byte identity below the bound: the shipped emission order INTERLEAVES modifications and change-file issues per summary (mod,issue,mod,issue) while three concatenated per-class lists emit mod,mod,issue,issue. ADOPTED SHAPE: ONE ordered hit list per region + three admission COUNTERS, so the admitted sequence is a subsequence of the shipped one BY CONSTRUCTION. Byte identity executed 5/5 including exactly-at-K. batch-63 standing design shape is therefore wrong.
phase1_result.design_correction_2: range_index.address_in_sorted_ranges is UNSOUND over overlapping ranges (inspects one bisect_right(starts,addr)-1 candidate, range_index.py:65-68) and returns bool so it can never name WHICH region; plus DeclaredRegion is inclusive while range_index is half-open, so without end+1 every region end address is a false negative. Found INDEPENDENTLY by both Phase-1 lanes and verified a third time by the orchestrator. LLR-103.2 workaround: coalesce to a disjoint half-open cover -> range_index becomes a SOUND O(log R) reject pre-filter; region identity from a caller-local bisect + prefix-max inside report_service.py. range_index.py untouched (frozen).
phase1_result.honest_scope: B-3(b) is REDUCED from RxVxE to VxE, NOT eliminated (candidates are unsorted lists with no address index, so one pass is irreducible). batch64_contribution_to_catalog: The catalog's meta-rule says the dominant defect class is the vacuous check and it concentrates in SPECS, not code. batch-64 adds a MEASURED nuance: its three instrument defects were not in the spec, they were in the FIXTURES and the MEASUREMENT WINDOWS. (a) AT-194's warm-up allocation landed inside its own first measured window, driving delta(2000) to -71485 and making its precondition unreachable. (b) TC-488's fixture carried 100 candidates per leaf against a cap of 200, so the per-class early exit the gate NAMED could not fire and the arm was dead. (c) FIX-E survives TC-487 by accident because both sub-fixtures are equal-start, so bisect_right lands on a candidate whose end still covers the probe. None was a product bug; all three were instrument bugs, and all three were found by EXECUTING the mutation rather than reading it. postmortem_headline: The orchestrator's standing frame — 'every post-Phase-1 defect was an instrument defect, not a product defect' — was REJECTED by the postmortem and replaced with: THE DESIGN WAS RIGHT AND THE DOCUMENT KEPT OUTRUNNING IT. The frame collapsed two classes that behave differently: ~14 OVER-CLAIMS (the document asserting a property the system does not have — R-independence false by a factor of R; 'the affected variants'; a scoping rule in shipped requirement text that was false about the report's own layout and would have made seven ATs permanently vacuous) and ~38 BLIND ORACLES (genuine instrument defects). Over-claiming is the exact sin the last three batches exist to stop, so calling it an instrument bug was too flattering. The causal link the frame hid: A CLAIM IS OVER-STATED EXACTLY WHERE NOTHING CAN FALSIFY IT — every over-claim sat on top of a missing or blind oracle. AND: part of 'no product defect' is a verdict the batch awarded itself. B-1/S1 was resolved by NARROWING THE REQUIREMENT, not fixing the structure; security offered 'keep the claim, fix the structure' as co-equal and never withdrew it. A = R x N is a real, executed, uncapped cost property of the shipped design, filed as a residual because the batch chose scope discipline. Right call, but it is a disposition, not an observation.
governance_watch_item: ELEVEN self-corrections across four agents, and ALL ELEVEN WEAKENED a finding. NOT ONE STRENGTHENED ONE. Two readings fit and the record cannot separate them: benign (reviewers over-reach by design, so calibration is one-directional, and every weakening here was execution-backed) versus concerning (this batch ran AUTONOMY + SELF-MERGE, and a reviewer who weakens their own finding removes an obstacle to a merge they also authorise). Filed as a WATCH-ITEM, not a conclusion. Cheap test for batch-65: did any reviewer ever ESCALATE their own prior finding after execution? Here, none did.
cost_verdict: The gates earned their keep; the artifact did not. Merging revision 1 ships a false R-independence claim with a gate structurally unable to notice it, plus seven silently-vacuous ATs — that justifies both gates. BUT three of the re-gate's most expensive findings were CREATED BY THE PREVIOUS FOLD: the batch spent a meaningful fraction of two gates reviewing damage it had just done to itself. THE LEVER IS A SMALLER DOCUMENT, NOT FEWER REVIEWS. ~14 agents was right for the risk and disproportionate to an artifact that was ours to size. 46 spec amendments, of which 40 repair the document's own prior claims; 6.1 spec lines per production line; ~1 spec defect per 75 spec lines; 75% of defect-finding effort spent on a document.
